newsitem.title: BRAZIL: INTERVIEW - Itau sees growth via insurance.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Itau sees growth via insurance.

text.p: With new investments in the booming insurance sector, Brazil's No. 2 private bank Banco Itau said it trusts it will grow sidestepping the market share battle that has shaken up the local banking industry.

Itau president Roberto Setubal said in a interview Itau is making a special effort this year to increase its presence in the insurance sector under its growth plans. But he added the bank is not getting involved with the war for clients that other retail banks are now immersed.

Banks have been desperately trying to lure new clients, designing new marketing strategies and products. Some are offering interest-free credit for overdrafts of up to 18 days. But Banco Itau prefers just to watch the competition.
"Other banks do not charge interest but they try to compensate it in other ways. We have another strategy," Setubal said.
Last month Itau, which already controlled a pension plan firm and a capitalization company, took over its sister Itau Seguros to consolidate its insurance and pension plan businesses.

In addition to targeting the insurance industry, Setubal said the bank aims to keep focusing on cutting expenses and offering high-quality services at lower costs just as it has been doing in the last few years.
Not even the arrival of Anglo-Asian financial giant HSBC Holdings Plc, which two months ago announced it had opened up for business in Brazil, has prompted Itau to review its plans.
"We are well prepared to face the competition with foreign banks. Newcomers will only make the local banking sector more solid," Setubal said.

Brazilian banking sector has become highly competitive after the Real stabilization plan put an end to the times of easy and high profits earned on large spreads. In the past, banks could make money without being concerned about expanding its client portfolio. But now with inflation tamed, higher productivity is key for the banks' survival.

The success of Itau's growth strategy, which has allowed it to boost its client base by 10 percent annually over the past four years, has been recognized internationally. Setubal said Itau is among the finalists competing to appear in the list of Top Emerging Market banks which is put together annually by Euromoney.

Itau ended last year with a net profit of 602 million reais, up 73 percent from 1995. In the first quarter of 1997, the bank showed a net income of 165 million reais, against a 143 million reais net profit a year ago.
With over four million clients, Banco Itau has sought to attract customers by charging competitive banking fees.
"Brazilians are thinking about changing banks because of the price they have to pay (for their services). The price/quality ratio has become an important factor," Setubal said.
But lower banking fees are just part of Itau's plans to satisfy clients. "In retail banking, it is not only one product, it is a combination of factors that sustains the client base," he said.

Itau has invested heavily in technology to attract new business and improve its relationship with clients. Setubal said the bank has installed 7,800 ATMs across the country performing over 45 million transactions a month.
Banco Itau also considers itself a "very accessible bank." Any individual with a minimum monthly income of 500 reais to 700 reais is allowed to open an account at the bank.

Setubal said Itau is also consolidating its expansion abroad. Itau, the first Brazilian bank to attack Argentina's retail sector, has a subsidiary in the country, with 19 branches. It plans to reach 35 branches in 1998.
In Europe, the bank's subsidiary Itau Europa, based in Portugal, has recently acquired a bank in Luxembourg in order to strengthen its private banking activities in the region.
